keyVerseText: Now in the first year of Cyrus king of Persia, that the word of the LORD spoken by the mouth of Jeremiah might be accomplished, the LORD stirred up the spirit of Cyrus king of Persia, that he made a proclamation throughout all his kingdom, and put it also in writing, saying,
rootMeaning: The name כּוֹרֶשׁ (Kôwresh) is the Hebrew form of the Persian name Cyrus, reflecting its foreign origin and royal stature. The etymology suggests a connection to the Persian root, possibly meaning 'possess thou the furnace,' which metaphorically may indicate strength or authority. This literal sense enriches our understanding by presenting Cyrus not merely as a historical figure but as one symbolizing powerful divine agency, a furnace of God's purpose in history.
usageInScripture: The word כּוֹרֶשׁ appears 15 times in the Hebrew Bible, consistently referring to the Persian king Cyrus. The top translations include 'of Cyrus' and 'Cyrus,' emphasizing his personal identity and royal role. His name is associated with the decree allowing Israelite exiles to return to Jerusalem, highlighting his unique place as a foreign ruler used by God to fulfill prophecy and restore His people.
theologicalSignificance: Theologically, כּוֹרֶשׁ embodies God's sovereignty over all nations, demonstrating that even a pagan king serves God's redemptive plan. Cyrus's role as the liberator of Israel underscores the truth that God's purposes transcend human boundaries and political powers. This reinforces the Christian conviction that God can raise up and use anyone to accomplish His will, foreshadowing the ultimate deliverance through Christ. Recognizing Cyrus as God's instrument invites believers to trust in God's providential control over history.
keyVerseReflection: 2 Chronicles 36:22 highlights that in Cyrus's first year as king of Persia, God stirred his spirit to issue a proclamation fulfilling Jeremiah's prophecy. The name כּוֹרֶשׁ here is central, emphasizing that this foreign king's actions were divinely inspired and pivotal in God's plan for Israel's restoration. This verse reveals that Cyrus is not merely a political figure but a chosen agent through whom God's word is realized.
